Task: Get the death certified — automatic if in hospital; otherwise contact the GP who attended
Get a Death Notification Form from the doctor who attended
Register the death with the local Registrar of Births, Marriages and Deaths (within 3 months; must be done within 12 months)
Order several copies of the death certificate (banks, pensions and insurers will each want their own)
Secure the property — locked, insured, perishables removed
Locate the will, if one exists, and identify the named executor(s)
Notify banks, building societies and credit unions (bring a death cert + proof of executor authority)
Notify pension providers and any life insurance policies
Notify Revenue (01 738 3600 or ros.ie) — a final income tax return may be needed for the year of death
Notify the mortgage provider, if applicable
Notify utility providers (electricity, gas, broadband, phone)
Cancel or transfer the Medical Card (HSE, 0818 22 44 78)
Notify the National Driver Licence Service (NDLS) if the person held a driving licence
Redirect or cancel post with An Post
Cancel subscriptions, memberships and direct debits once accounts are formally closed

Decide: personal application (most estates) or instruct a solicitor (required if there's a dispute, the will is lost, the applicant is under 18, the deceased lived outside Ireland, or a non-resident applicant with beneficiaries other than a spouse inheriting EUR 20,000+)
File the Statement of Affairs (Form SA.2) with Revenue
Complete the Personal Application Form (or, via a solicitor: Form S1 + Executor's Oath + Inland Revenue Affidavit CA24)
Submit the application and supporting documents to the correct Probate Office (Dublin Probate Office for Dublin/Kildare/Meath/Wicklow; Dublin or your county's District Probate Registry otherwise)
Attend the Probate Office appointment to swear the oath and have documents examined (personal applicants)
Receive the Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there's no will)
Register the Grant with each bank, pension provider and insurer to release funds
Pay any Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) due and file an IT38 return via ROS if required
Settle outstanding debts and expenses from the estate
Transfer or sell property as needed — this is usually when a house clearance is arranged
Distribute the remaining estate to beneficiaries as set out in the will (or under intestacy rules)

This checklist is a general starting point, not legal or tax advice — every estate is different. Confirm your specific situation with a solicitor or accountant, especially around probate requirements and CAT liability.
